posts.text:
My NFL Today’s Picks (Week 7 – 2026 Season)

What in the wide world of sports is going on here in the NFL. I mean we got headlines up and down the line here, heck I do not even know where to begin. However, the NFL is going to let the Philadelphia Eagles off the hook, at least for now. The Eagles will not have Quarterback Jalen Hurts for the remainer of this season due to blood clots in his leg. But this is not completely over by a long shot here. I hope this is not the end for Jalen Hurts, but I wish him well on his recovery. The New York Giants will have a new quarterback under center this Sunday. Its none other than J.J. McCarthy, who was obtained in a trade with the Minnesota Vikings. The Giants surprising everyone with there lead in the NFC East Division, in spite of losing to those New Orleans Saints. So where in the world is there running game, you cannot find it at all. Even if the Giants make the playoffs somehow, they may not last too long this postseason. They might be one and done quicker than a typical college basketball player. By the way, there are still 2 teams winless on the season. Oh you thought we were kidding? Well the Miami Dolphins (0-5) and the Los Angeles Chargers (0-6) have more issues than a love shack on a summer boring day. Well as for my NFL picks so far, another good week as we wind down the month of October. The season is almost coming to its midpoint of the regular season as we head into Week 7. In Week 6, I went 9-5 to add to my monthly totals in being 30-14-1 in October. On the 2026 season so far, I am 56-36-1 as another great week of NFL games is coming our way. By trading J.J. McCarthy now, the Vikings save over $4.6M in cash and cap space and get an unconditional fifth-round pick in the next draft that, depending how the Giants finish, could end up being a top-150 selection.

posts.author: tompelissero.bsky.social
posts.text:
Trade! The Vikings are sending QB J.J. McCarthy to the Giants for a 2027 fifth-round pick, sources tell The Ringer and Netflix Sports.

Reddit's public JSON endpoints have contested availability in 2026 (some reports say ~60 req/min unauthenticated, others say broadly blocked with 403 since May 2026), so an unreachable probe here is expected and is not treated as a pipeline failure.
